articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Mill Hill
articles.deck: Residents of Mill Hill filled the hall on Sunday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings. Esther Nakamura, who has lived in Mill Hill for 16 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The plan calls for book exchange box along Linden Terrace, with work expected to start in November. The Mill Hill Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Public works estimates the work will take about 16 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Stonebridge Volunteers Host Spring Drive
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 36 people and say second recycling drop-off is the main draw.
body: The effort began in June when a handful of neighbors met at St. Brendan’s hall to talk about second recycling drop-off. The Stonebridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Council Approves $12,000 for Warren Avenue Repairs
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Warren Avenue disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 14 weeks once it starts in June. Residents of Kettle Hill said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Councilmember Brian Bruckner asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000.

articles.title: Margaret Kozak, 72, Church Organist
articles.deck: Friends remember Margaret Kozak for the many years of service to Hickory Ridge.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Hickory Ridge.
Born in Hickory Ridge in the years after the war, Margaret Kozak spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Margaret Kozak died in May at home on Quincy Avenue, at the age of 72. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program in his or her name.

articles.title: Letter: Support the After-school Reading Program
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the September meeting.

Please keep the after-school reading program in the budget. Many of us on Linden Court use it every week. To the editor: I have lived on Linden Court for 18 years, and I want to say what a difference Scout Troop 14 has made.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the September meeting.
Albert Dunmore, Upper Commons
